fix(traceback): drop the bug note that this change resolves

The comment in `src/node/traceback.ts` recorded that width came from
stdout regardless of `stderr: true` and pointed at rich-console-ujo, the
open ticket tracking that defect. Selecting the bound stream once closes
that ticket, so the note now describes behaviour that no longer exists.

Deleted rather than re-pointed. The colour-depth sentence above it stays
because it explains something the code cannot — why `beginCapture` is
used instead of a `file:` sink. Width following the stream the console is
bound to needs no comment; it is only worth remarking on when it isn't
true.

feat(console): take the host environment by injection (rich-seam-981.3)

`src/core/console.ts` asked the host four questions — is this a terminal,
how wide, how tall, where do bytes go — and each one re-derived its own
answer from ambient `process` behind its own `typeof` guard. Safe by
repeated care rather than by construction, and the care had already
lapsed: three sites selected the stream with `stderr ? stderr : stdout`
and the fourth, size detection, did not.

`ConsoleOptions` now takes an `environment` carrying `env` plus both
streams, resolved once at construction into the single stream the console
is bound to. Node's `process` satisfies `ConsoleEnvironment` structurally,
so it remains the default with no adapter at either end, and there is
exactly one read of the ambient global in the module.

Selecting the stream once is also what fixes rich-console-ujo /
rich-width-3cf.4: colour, dimensions, and the output sink now come from
the same stream, so `Console({ stderr: true })` reports stderr's width.

`isTerminal` collapses to a field — every input to it is fixed at
construction — which removes the getter that mirrored `effectiveIsTTY`,
along with the `_stderr` and `_forceTerminal` fields that existed only to
feed it.

Verified with `process` genuinely absent: `delete globalThis.process`,
then a Console driven entirely from an injected environment reports
100x30, truecolor, isTerminal true, and writes into a captured array;
a console whose environment has no streams throws the documented error.
Both new stream-binding tests were falsified by reverting the selection
to stdout-only, and the env-precedence test by ignoring the injected env.

feat(seam): move NodeTerminalHost behind the node subpath (rich-seam-981.2) (#71)

* feat(seam): move NodeTerminalHost behind the node subpath (rich-seam-981.2)

`NodeTerminalHost` read `process.stdin` / `process.stdout` from
`src/widgets/terminal-host.ts`, which is reachable from the main barrel.
The read is inside the constructor, so importing the barrel in a browser
never threw — the browser-safe guarantee held by care rather than by
construction, the same shape rich-seam-981.1 fixed for the traceback
installer.

The class, its options type, and its private `NodeReadable` /
`NodeWritable` stream shapes now live in `src/node/terminal-host.ts`
behind a `./node/terminal-host` export entry. `TerminalHost`,
`TerminalSize`, and `BrowserTerminalHost` stay in the barrel: the
interface is the seam and belongs everywhere; only the implementation
that touches the ambient global is node-only. The dependency runs one
way — the node adapter imports the seam, nothing in the barrel imports
the adapter.

Measured rather than assumed: walking the built module graph from
`dist/index.js` (90 modules) leaves no unguarded `process` reference
reachable from the barrel. What remains is comments plus the
`typeof process === "undefined"`-guarded sites in `core/color.ts` and
`core/console.ts`, which rich-seam-981.3 owns. That closes the last
unguarded site the epic names.

Repaired two maps this change would otherwise have left lying:

- `src/widgets/terminal-host.ts`'s header claimed to be "the single owner
  of node TTY access in the codebase" and named itself as the node host's
  home. Both became false. The replacement states the dependency
  direction instead — a claim the compiler keeps. (The separate
  contradiction with `core/console.ts`'s TTY fallback is rich-seam-981.6.)
- `CLAUDE.md` said `src/node/` was "two files, two package subpaths"; it
  was already four after #70. It now points at `package.json#exports` as
  the list rather than restating it.

Verification, each check falsified before being trusted:

- Adding a throwaway export to the new subpath made the coverage gate
  fail naming it and its file, so the gate genuinely sees the new entry
  module; removing it restored green.
- Node package self-reference resolves the real `exports` map:
  `@promptctl/rich-js/node/terminal-host` yields the class, and the
  barrel yields `undefined`. `tsc` alone would not have caught a typo in
  the `exports` target.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (1787 passing), `npm run docs:build`,
  `npm run test:demos` (10/10 browser demos boot), and a live run of the
  `rich-strip` node demo from `dist-demo/`.

Note for the next reader: `npm run lint` does not type-check `examples/`.
A missed demo import survived lint and was caught only by the coverage
verifier's `assertProgramClean`.

* docs(widgets): delete the cross-reference this move invalidated

`XtermTerminal`'s JSDoc pointed at `NodeReadable`/`NodeWritable` "above" as
a second example of declaring a dependency by shape. This PR moved both
interfaces to `src/node/terminal-host.ts`, so "above" points at nothing.

Deleted rather than re-pointed. Re-pointing would swap a stale intra-file
reference for a cross-file one across the package seam, where the next
agent editing the node adapter has no reason to grep this file — the same
rot with a longer fuse. The surrounding paragraph already states the whole
rationale in full; "same idea as X" only pointed at a second instance of a
rule the sentence had just given, so deleting it costs a reader nothing and
removes one more claim that has to stay true.
